sermon.title: UnBorn Again
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In “UnBorn Again,” Pastor David G. Kincer uses the stages of a seed, an embryo and a baby to teach spiritual growth. He covers how hearing the word starts the process, why some “abort” it (mock it or put it off), the four soils, baptism, and what it means to grow up into Christ rather than a denomination.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: he gives “Acts 24:5” where the passage he describes is Acts 24:25, and says “Of the 15 apostles” (there were twelve). He reads Galatians 4:19 as “until [unclear] be formed in you.” He names several public figures in a list of people not to follow; the captions garble two of the names and they are shown as [unclear]. The captions also garble a few words about the Holy Spirit’s power and the end-times terms “pre-trib” and “amillennial.” He makes strong political statements (a federal bill he says the Senate passed, welfare, homosexuality, abortion and liberals); these are his own views and describe events as of 2013–2014.

chunks.section_question: What does natural growth from a seed teach about spiritual growth?
chunks.short_answer: He says “the Bible always uses natural illustrations to help us understand the spiritual.” Every seed has an embryo that grows “into the image that God designed it to grow in,” and in the spirit “the word of God is what’s going to start that seed in us.”
chunks.text:
Today we are going to talk about spiritual growth. All right, as you can see up there, I have some photos illustrating the natural, spiritual growth. At the top, the baby in the womb, the baby born, and then toddler up to adulthood. And then in the second series, we have, again, the baby in the womb, the baby born, and then following Jesus, growing to maturity. And this is what this is about. And the Bible always uses natural illustrations to help us understand the spiritual. Here we have a seed. Inside every seed is an embryo, okay, that embryo contains life. All it has to do is have the water to hit that seed, after that seed is dead, and that embryo inside will start growing into the image that God designed it to grow in. A bean will not produce a tomato. It will grow into the image.

As you can see, the roots start coming out, the root more, and then the plant starts growing out of the ground, and then the leaves start growing on the plant, and in the end you have the fruit of that plant, and that is the growing process. Also in the spirit, we need a seed. See, we need it watered, we need it in the right atmosphere, the right conditions, and the word of God is what’s going to start that seed in us. It’s going to be the embryo, all right.

chunks.section_question: What is the “unborn” stage of spiritual growth, and what happens when we hear the word? (Acts 17:32)
chunks.short_answer: He says the unborn stage is when God’s word is planted “in your inner man.” Some who heard Paul “mocked,” some said “we’ll hear you again,” and “some believed and followed.” He says “when you mock and when you want to put it off, you have hindered the growth of the word.”
chunks.text:
Now we’re going to look at the unborn fetus stage of growth, okay, and how to recognize an unborn seed of God’s word. It’s in the fetus stage, all right. Acts 17:32, “when they heard of the resurrection of the dead.” Okay, they heard. God has chosen the foolishness of preaching to save all that would believe. You know, go out and preach the gospel, and so that is the sowing of the word. When you hear the word, that’s when God will come by his Spirit and try to plant that word in your inner man, in your spirit. We got it. You young ones over here, got it? See, hearing the word is vitally important. All right, “when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked.” See, they didn’t let the word take, get attached to the spiritual man and grow. “Others said, we’ll hear you again.”

They put it off. Well, you know, I’m busy, you know, I’m getting a career, I’m going to college, I’m working, I’m raising kids, whatever. You know, I’ll listen another time. “But some believed and followed.” So which ones actually let the embryo grow and produce seed? The one who believed, and not just believed, but they followed. All right, when you mock, and when you want to put it off, you have hindered the growth of the word in your inner man. They didn’t mock and they didn’t put it off. They said, “What must we do?”

chunks.section_question: How did the jailer respond to the word, and why does he say baptism should not be delayed? (Acts 2:37; 16:25-33)
chunks.short_answer: He says the jailer “trembled,” asked “what must I do to be saved,” and was baptized “the same night.” He says he asked a nation that delays baptism six months to a year for “scripture for putting off baptism” and “there is none,” and that baptism is not “an outward sign of an inward work.”
chunks.text:
And so the embryo is getting root and growing in. Acts 16:25-29: Paul and Silas were in jail, and they prayed and sang praises to God, the prisoners what? Heard them. They didn’t do silent prayers. They didn’t do silent praise and worship. The prisoners heard them. All right, then the keeper of the prison was going to kill himself, and Paul said, “Don’t do that. Don’t kill yourself. We’re all here. There’s no one escaped.” And so when the keeper heard, what did he do? He trembled. See, the word affected him. It shook him, it stirred him. He trembled at the word of the Lord, fell down and said, “What must I do to be saved?” See, we knew he heard the message because he’s asking, “What do I got to do to correct my problem, to get saved from sin? What do I got to do?” And the word pierced his heart.

That embryo started, that seed started. He didn’t mock, he didn’t put it off. He let it bring forth that embryo fruit, the root starting and the fruit of salvation to be produced in his life. You got it? Acts 16:33: “The same hour of the night he was baptized in all his house, immediately, and rejoiced, believing in God with all his house.”

I was just in a nation not too long ago where they put off baptism for six months to a year, and I asked them, “Give me scripture for putting off baptism.” There is none. You repent and you what? Get baptized. How long did it take for the jail keeper to get baptized in water? The same night. You see why? Because baptism is not a ceremony, which I heard recently, an outward sign of an inward work. That is not in the Bible. You cannot show me that statement in the Bible. It’s just something we hear and we hold on to it and we repeat it without really checking in the Bible. Baptism is putting to death of the old man of sin and coming up a new creature, and people need to know this stuff before they’re baptized so that they can experience baptism for what it’s for.

Can I hear an amen? And a lot of people have been robbed of a great experience in water baptism because it’s an outward sign of an inward work, we’re just going through a ceremony, it’s just a ritual, there’s nothing in it. There is something in it. When you put to death the old man, there’s something powerful happening, and when you rise up a new creature that’s committed to righteousness, that is a tremendous work of God, and God chose water baptism to do that.

chunks.section_question: What are the four kinds of ground in the parable of the sower, and what does he add about patience? (Matthew 13)
chunks.short_answer: He describes hard-minded hearers who “mocked” and “put it off,” the skeptical who “have no root” and “fall away,” those “choked” by the cares of life, and the “honest and good heart” who “keep the word.” He says we need many seeds of the word, not just “grace and faith or water baptism,” and “patience for God to reveal … the truth.”
chunks.text:
Now we’re going to go to the old Sunday school lesson of the parable of the sower. The seeds fell on four different kinds of ground, four different kinds of hearers. This helps us to understand the embryo growth, the embryo, that initial inward growth of God. All right, the seed fell on the wayside here, or it fell on hard minds, okay. Their minds were hardened. They hear, then comes the Devil and takes away the word. They mocked, they put it off, see, like we already heard, “lest they should believe and be saved.” They never get to the believing stage, that never brings forth the fruit of trusting God. Believe is to trust. All right, that’s the first one. They’re hard-hearted, they’re hard-headed, they’re hard-minded, and they mock and they don’t listen to the word of God. The second one fell upon the rocks. They’re the skeptical ones, the doubters.

They hear and receive the word with joy, but they have no root. And who’s the root? Jesus Christ is the root and offspring of David. They have no root in themselves, and in time of temptation they fall away. You see, time of testing they fall away. Now, a lot of churches preach that Christians don’t go through testing. Show me in the Bible. And no, don’t just preach stuff, show me, because I can show you from Adam to John the Revelator testings, and you’re going to go through testings, all right. They fall away. What do they fall away from? The only thing they had. What did they have? Belief. They fall away from the belief. Okay, and oh, these are the, I call them shooting stars. They get saved and they put on these great things. “Oh yeah, man, oh what, you know, I was in drugs and I was a prostitute and all this stuff and man, I got saved, Jesus saved me and old man,” and then poof, they’re gone, because there’s no root.

The root can’t grow on rocks. The rocks are too hard, it can’t find a place to get into the soil and bring forth fruit. Number three, they fell among thorns. These people hear the word of God and they go forth and are choked. They go forth, they go out into the world, they live their life (and all of us have got to go out into the world and live our life), and they’re choked with the cares and the riches and pleasures of this life and bring no fruit to perfection or maturity. They got a little bit of faith, see, they got a little bit of grace, got a little bit of, you know, belief, but never brings it to maturity where it really can be seen in their life. And this is the embryo again. See, the embryo is not growing right. That inner seed is not growing right.

And then some fell on good ground. These are they that hear the word in an honest and good heart. They’re not hiding any sins, they’re not hiding any pride, they’re not hiding anything. They have an honest heart. If they make a mistake, they admit it, and their heart, their mind is set to do good. You see, they repented because they were doing bad things, and they have a goal to do good things, and so out of that kind of mind, out of that kind of an emotion, the embryo seed can grow, get root and produce fruit. See, and they heard the word, they keep the word. They actually keep the word. They don’t just talk about faith and grace, they keep the word. Every word that they heard, they set a goal to keep.

Isn’t that beautiful? And how many you know there’s more word in the Bible than just saved by grace through faith. That is the initial foundation that you must get started on, but there’s a lot of word seed. All of you, I’m sure, enjoy different vegetables, not just wheat. You don’t go through life just eating wheat all the time. You throw a little corn, beans in there, and potatoes and rice, and so it is in the word of God. There are many seeds of the word, and you need them all for nourishment. Wow, that was good. Did you guys get that? We can’t stop at grace and faith or water baptism. Okay, and they bring forth fruit with what? What’s that magic word? Patience. You know, they don’t give up because they’re not there yet. They don’t quit because they haven’t bridled the tongue yet. They don’t quit because they haven’t bridled their temper yet.

They don’t quit because, you know, they haven’t figured out what the Holy Ghost baptism is all about. They don’t quit because they don’t know which way Christ is coming: [unclear] post-trib, mid-trib, [unclear] millennium, postmillennium, premillennium. You know, they don’t quit and give up, they just keep growing. They have patience for God to reveal to them the truth, and that’s the only way you’re going to get it anyway. There is no preacher that has the power to open your spiritual man to understand the word. Only the Holy Ghost can do that.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then He spoke many things to them in parables, saying: “Behold, a sower went out to sow. And as he sowed, some seed fell by the wayside; and the birds came and devoured them. Some fell on stony places, where they did not have much earth; and they immediately sprang up because they had no depth of earth. But when the sun was up they were scorched, and because they had no root they withered away. And some fell among thorns, and the thorns sprang up and choked them. But others fell on good ground and yielded a crop: some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty. He who has ears to hear, let him hear!”
Those by the wayside are the ones who hear; then the devil comes and takes away the word out of their hearts, lest they should believe and be saved.
But the ones that fell on the good ground are those who, having heard the word with a noble and good heart, keep it and bear fruit with patience.

chunks.section_question: What does he mean by people who “abort the word”? (Acts 5:33; 7:54; 24:25)
chunks.short_answer: He says some people in the Bible “aborted the word,” killing it “just like a baby,” and then tried “to shut up anybody that’s speaking the truth.” He gives the council that wanted to slay the apostles, those who stoned Stephen, and Felix, who trembled when Paul reasoned of righteousness, self-control and judgment.
chunks.text:
We’re going to look at people that abort the word and their reaction, their behavior. All right, these are people that are in the Bible that aborted the word. We’re going to Acts. We’ll start with Acts 5:33: “When they heard, they were cut to the heart and took counsel to slay” Peter and the apostles who spoke the word. See, they not only mock, they don’t even put it off for another day, they not only mock but they want to physically address the issue. And you got to understand why these people are the way they are. They aborted the word. The word came, they killed it, just like a baby. This baby has been killed and aborted by a saline solution. They just burn the baby to death. And this is what people do with the word. They just kill it, and then when they kill it, their outward behavior is to try to shut up anybody that’s speaking the truth of God’s word.

Acts 7:54: “When they heard these things, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed on him with their teeth” and stoned Stephen. You see, again, they aborted the word. He gave them a tremendous word. As you know, one of the greatest sermons ever. You talking about me preaching from Genesis to Revelation, this guy covered half of the Old Testament in one sermon, and instead of them going, “Yay for Jesus, yay for truth,” they aborted the word. The Bible says they put their hands over their ears, they hated it, and they stoned Stephen. Acts 24:5: as Paul reasoned to Felix, the civil leader, as he reasoned, that’s him preaching the word, he’s talking the word, he reasoned of righteousness, temperance or self-control, and the judgment to come. He said there’s a coming judgment if you don’t control yourself and do what’s right, and the word caused Felix to what?

Tremble. I’ve told you before, I have witnessed to atheists. Atheists say, “You cannot prove there’s a God.” I tell them, “I can prove there’s a God.” They go, “Oh no, you can’t.” I said, “Oh yes, I can.” And I said, “If you obey the principles of this book, you admit you’re sinners, you ask Jesus to forgive you your sins, and you will find God showing up and making himself real.” And so they go through the motions, okay, and those of course, they don’t know how to pray, so I’ll say, “You know, just follow my prayer, just repeat after me,” and man, you know, I bring out the sin, and I’m specific with the sins, and they’re speaking, “I’m over there arrogant,” and all this stuff. Oh yeah, yeah. And then I asked them to ask Jesus to cleanse them for these sins, and man, when they start saying that part, they start shaking.

They don’t want it to be real. They don’t want this presence to be there, and so they resisted. And this is what people in the baptized in the Holy Ghost do. The reason they shake is because they don’t know how to release the baptism of the Holy Ghost, and I was a shaker until I learned how to channel it. You know, this power comes on you and you go, “My goodness, whoa.” You like it but you’re afraid of it, and you kind of, oo. And this is what the atheists did. They tremble, and then they let go of my hand, “We got to get out of here.” And Mr. Barnes has been with me at least twice when I’ve done that, haven’t you? See, God honors his word. God shows up. Don’t tell me I can’t prove there’s a God. God will honor his word. Hallelujah.

chunks.section_question: How do we grow into Christ and not into a denomination? (Mark 4:26; Ephesians 4:15; Galatians 4:19)
chunks.short_answer: He says the seed is the word of God, the field is the world, and the fruit comes “first the blade, then the head.” He says “we grow up into Christ,” not a denomination: “God isn’t out to form any denomination in us. He’s out to form Christ in us,” and we are to “imitate the image of his Son.”
chunks.text:
We’ve got to grow in this embryo, this inner stage. You see, before this outward fruit’s going to come out, we got to grow in this inward stage to imitate Christ. Mark 4:26: “The kingdom of God is as if a man should scatter seed on the ground, and sleep by night and rise by day, and the seed should sprout and grow.” Okay, Luke 8:11 tells us the seed is the word of God. What’s the seed? The word of God, and it has to be spoken, it has to be preached. And the field, in Matthew 13:38, is the world. What’s the field? The seed is grown in the world, mankind. Say mankind. Mankind. See, we got to get the word out for people to hear it, whether they like it or not. Could that be an amen? Because that is essential to them changing. “For the earth yields crops by itself, first the blade, then the head, and after that the full grain of the head,” the mature fruit, just like the seed that was planted was.

“And when the grain ripens, immediately the harvest has come.” Ephesians 4:15: “Speak the truth in love, and you will grow up in all things unto him who is the head.” We grow up into all things unto who? Jesus. Not the pope, not Billy Graham, not [unclear] Roberts, not Joel [unclear], but we grow up into Christ. Not our denomination, not being an independent church or a denominate. We got to grow up into who? Jesus Christ. That’s the full grain, Jesus. He’s the seed that was planted. See, that inner growth is very important, and that’s why a lot of us don’t have outward growth, is because we haven’t dealt with the inward. Galatians 4:19: “I travailed in birth again until [unclear] be formed in you.” Okay, Baptist be formed in you? No. Pentecostal be formed in you? No. Folks, God isn’t out to form any denomination in us.

He’s out to form Christ in us. See, shape Christ in us. Christ starts as an inward embryo in our spiritual man, and we have to cultivate it, feed it for it to grow. Romans 8:29: “For whom he did foreknow he also did predestinate to be conformed” (to imitate; the word conformed is imitate) “the image of his Son.” Now, is that clear? You see, we’re on a growing process.

chunks.section_question: Is every stage of growth “perfect,” and what would Christ not do? (Pentecostal practices, doctors)
chunks.short_answer: He says “every stage of God’s growth to him is perfect,” so a baby Christian is fine, but staying a baby is the problem. He says Christ would not abuse his family, “handle snakes and drink poison to show their faith,” or say “you can’t go to the doctor,” because Jesus said the sick “need a physician,” and he calls literal hand-cutting an “allegory.”
chunks.text:
Now see, the atheists pick on us because we are in growing processes. You know, we’re not there yet. We call ourselves Christians because we’re babies, but there are a lot of things we haven’t grown up in, and people attack us for not being a grown-up Christian. But if you know what stage you’re in, every stage of God’s growth to him is perfect. Amen. If you’re a baby, you’re a baby, there’s nothing wrong with that. We all got to be spiritual babies. If you’re just an embryo trying to break out and bring forth that seed of Christ and all that, there’s nothing wrong with that. You are birthing that seed, there’s nothing wrong with that. People can laugh at you, mock you if they want, but God looks at you and says that person is perfect. Why? Because they’re right where they’re supposed to be at this time.

Hallelujah. And so many Christians give up because the word isn’t made plain to them and they think it’s impossible. No, everywhere you’re at, God sees it as perfection. Why? Because that’s exactly where you should be. Let me ask you this. Would Christ abuse or mistreat and be cruel to children? No. Would Christ abuse their spouse, mistreat them? No. So what’s the problem with this divorce and these family problems in the church world? What is the problem? The embryo hasn’t been developed right. They are following a religion, a philosophy, an idea, instead of Christ. Do you see that? Yeah, they blame everything else, but the real problem is they have got to respond to that word in their spiritual man, because Christ would not do that. They wouldn’t handle snakes and drink poison to show their faith. Christ wouldn’t do that. Christ would not say, “Well, you’re sick, you can’t go to the doctor, or you don’t have faith.”

Would he? No. Jesus himself said, “They that are sick need a physician.” Yes, God can heal, but if he doesn’t, you better get to a doctor. Jesus himself said, if you’re sick you need a physician. So this is a lot in the Pentecostal areas. They just make us look stupid, these people with this nonsense. “Cut off your hand or pluck out your eye.” The Bible says, you know, better to pluck your hand off and pluck out your eye and let it, you cause you to sin. That is an allegory, idiot. Jesus never went around cutting off people’s hands. He didn’t go around plucking out people’s eyes, neither the apostles. You see, these are ignorant people that twist the Scriptures to their own destruction, which we already showed you, and you got to follow Christ. You got to realize that Christ would do certain things and wouldn’t do certain things, and when you’re doing things Christ wouldn’t do, that tells you you’re wrong. Amen.

chunks.section_question: What are the “seeds” to add to faith, and why give God one hour a day? (1 Peter 1:23; 2 Peter 1)
chunks.short_answer: He says we are “being born again by the … word of God,” and all the seeds of the word are needed, including repentance, baptism and the Holy Spirit. He says these are “kindergarten doctrines” and we must add “virtue” and “knowledge,” and “we won’t give God one hour a day in the Bible and in prayer.”
chunks.text:
You see, all of these is a seed of the word, and you need all the seeds growing in your life to be a complete Christian. Are you with me? Let’s continue. Then we go over to Second Peter, and we find we add to our faith virtue, or good morals, justice. Should Christians stand for justice, for goodness, for right? Yes. That’s the “add to your faith virtue.” You say, we like to stay over here in the second coming, and oh, we argue and quarrel about water baptism and Holy Spirit baptism and baptism of the body. We haven’t even, we quarrel over those things, and those things the Bible says are kindergarten doctrines. They’re the first principles of God, they’re not deep stuff at all. Everybody thinks the second coming is deep. Yeah, you talk about the Holy Ghost, deep. No, the Bible says these are kindergarten, first grade doctrines, primary doctrines.

You got to go on to the character doctrines: virtue, good morals.

Knowledge, knowledge of the Scriptures. Jesus said, “You do err, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God.” You see, we need to know the Scriptures. “My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.” And we won’t give God one hour a day in the Bible and in prayer to get knowledge. It just floors me. He asked for one hour. One hour, sixty minutes, and we got time to watch everything on TV, we got time to play sports, we got time to hang glide, we got time to surf, we got time to do all this. “Oh, I’m so busy.” You’re busy satisfying your own agenda. God asks for one hour of your day and you’re not giving it to him. That’s how you grow to be good, that’s how you grow in knowledge. You got to be in the word and pray the word. Forget this “now I lay me down to sleep” stuff.

Pray the word. Self-control: we got to grow into controlling ourselves, and the reason we won’t give God one hour a day is we lack self-control. Patience. You see, now we’re climbing the ladder. I mean, these are big things. See, God has an organized structure. Self-control and patience are big fruits. Love your enemy. Love God, love the right believer. Jesus said, “A new commandment I give unto you, that you love one another.” I got to love myself, and I got to love my family, I got to love my wife, I got to love my kids, I can’t hurt them, and love is the goal. The high mark of the calling of God is to love God, love his word, love people, and do nothing to harm them. And we’re way down the ladder. Most of us are back here with these two, grace and faith. That’s as far as we go.

chunks.section_question: What comes after knowledge: self-control, patience and love? (John 13:34; Romans 1:17; 2 Corinthians 1:10)
chunks.short_answer: He says “self-control and patience are big fruits” and “love is the goal,” the “high mark of the calling of God.” He says righteousness is revealed “from faith to faith,” that being filled with the Holy Ghost did not end his problems, and that God is “in the midst of delivering us.”
chunks.text:
How many would raise your hand and say, “Lord, give me some more embryos”? If you don’t ask, you don’t get. Now, how many were raised? “Lord, I want more embryos. Yeah, I want them growing.” Listen now, how many will give him one hour a day to let that happen? Uh-huh. Now, now we’re getting somewhere.

Romans 1:17. You got to understand this now. You young ones, pay attention here. This is really good, because Satan really likes to get on you young ones, because the Bible says flee youthful lust. There’s certain lust of the flesh that youth have because they’re growing into adulthood. All right, “the righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith.” So what should my faith be doing? Bringing me into the righteous character of Christ, one seed at a time. Yes, I might not have self-control yet, but God said he’s going to reveal it as I respond to the previous doctrines. I will get that patience, I will get that self-control. Are you there? See, it’s a growing process. When I got saved in Pentecostal churches, man, they said if you got filled with the Holy Ghost, bang, your problems were over. I got filled with the Holy Ghost and bam, I had more problems.

I didn’t even know I had problems before he came along and shined light on them. Man, and I had to work through these things. There was no [unclear] power [unclear], man, just got me through some of these trials and tribulations and growth things. I had to work the work of faith, I had to pursue knowledge, I had to pursue Christ to get through them. 2 Corinthians 1:10: “Who delivered us from so great a death, and does deliver us, in whom we trust that he will still deliver us.” That great death is what? The wages of sin. He delivers us. See, but he is in the midst of delivering us, and tomorrow he’ll be there to still deliver you. Why? Because you need to grow, and you’re violating God’s inheritance, God’s commandments, in certain areas, and so you need deliverance on the way up to that top fruit of love.

I can’t make it more clear than that. And remember, every stage in God is perfect, but when you are a baby when you should be a child or a young adult in God, that’s the problem, as we will see as we pursue this. Are you with me? But we need to get the inner right. Okay, the word delivers us and sets us free from sin, sets us free to do right and obey truth.

chunks.section_question: Are we the “glorious church” yet, and why must we get the word out? (Ezekiel 14:14)
chunks.short_answer: He says Noah, Job and Daniel were saved by their own righteousness, and “I can’t be saved because my mom and dad were righteous.” He says the church is not yet the glorious church because “we can’t even fellowship with people outside of our corral,” that “who much is given, much is required,” and that the word must go out “printed word, audio word, video word, any word.”
chunks.text:
Noah, Job and Daniel are mentioned in God’s hall of fame in Ezekiel 14:14, and what was the only thing that would save them from wars, earthquakes, plagues? Their righteousness. You got it? You got it. I can’t be saved because my mom and dad were righteous. I can’t be saved because the pope is righteous. I can’t be saved because Billy Graham is righteous. I got to be, I will be saved because I have been birthed in Christ and I’m growing in him, and I’m at the stage where I’m at, and God sees it as perfect and saves me so I can go on to the next stage. See, growth is a stage, there, steps. End-time prophets look at Israel, they look at acts of God, they look at wickedness, instead of the glorious church overcoming the gates of hell. The Bible says in Revelation that he’s coming and his bride has what?

Made herself ready. Ephesians says that he’s coming for a bride that is a glorious church without spot or wrinkle or any such thing. Are we there yet? No, we can’t even fellowship with people outside of our corral, our denomination, our beliefs. We’re not there. Are we destroying the gates of hell in America today as a corporate church? No way. The homosexuals, the atheists, everybody’s having free rein with us. You’re going to be sad that you were here this morning, because who much is given, much is required. Church, God has given this church a fantastic word, but if we don’t take it seriously and get it out to others and just live our life, grazing, kids, working a job, going through every day routine, we’re not going to help anybody. So I submit to you, we got to get the word out, and get them to hear the word and read the word.

That word will set people free, that word will heal people, but we can’t keep putting it off. We can’t just stay at this place where, “Oh boy, we got a word, hallelujah, that was a good message.” No, we’ve got to get a hunger and desire and a compelling to get it out to others. Could that be an amen? Printed word, audio word, video word, any word, we need to get it out, because it’s the word that sets us free, and who much is given, much is required, and we need to get this word out. We need to challenge. I’m ready to get on radio and TV and challenge the leaders of our day, both political and church leaders. They are wimps when they deny the truth of the Bible just to have a big congregation and a lavish lifestyle. That is wrong. We need to preach truth no matter if it takes everything, every possession we got.

faqs.answer: He calls the rocky-ground hearers “shooting stars”: they “get saved and they put on these great things,” and “then poof, they’re gone, because there’s no root.” He also says “a lot of churches preach that Christians don’t go through testing.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Those by the wayside are the ones who hear; then the devil comes and takes away the word out of their hearts, lest they should believe and be saved.

faqs.question: What does he say “good ground” looks like?
faqs.answer: He says they have “an honest heart,” “they’re not hiding any sins,” “if they make a mistake, they admit it,” and “they keep the word.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: But the ones that fell on the good ground are those who, having heard the word with a noble and good heart, keep it and bear fruit with patience.

faqs.question: What does he say happens when he witnesses to atheists?
faqs.answer: He says he tells them “I can prove there’s a God” if they “obey the principles of this book,” and that when they pray about their sins “they start shaking” and “don’t want it to be real.”

faqs.question: Why does he compare rejecting the word to abortion?
faqs.answer: He says Felix “aborted the word” after he “shook and he trembled,” “just like people abort babies today. They don’t want them, they’re inconvenient, and they abort them.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you do believe.”

faqs.question: What does he say the word “Christian” means?
faqs.answer: He says the suffix “ian” means “to come from, belong to, or to follow,” so “a Christian follows Christ, period,” not “a Protestant denomination.” He says “I can be a Pentecostal, I can be a Baptist, I can be a Methodist, I can be a Catholic and follow Christ.”

faqs.question: What does he say happened in 1968?
faqs.answer: He says “God poured out the Holy Ghost upon all the denominations,” and the denominations “kicked them out,” though the Catholics said “go ahead, do your thing in the back room.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: “These things I have spoken to you, that you should not be made to stumble. They will put you out of the synagogues; yes, the time is coming that whoever kills you will think that he offers God service.

faqs.question: What does he mean by a “religionist”?
faqs.answer: He says “religionist is someone that puts their opinions above the Scripture,” and “when you put your opinions or your denomination’s opinions above Scripture, you are a religionist.”

faqs.question: Does he say being a baby Christian is a problem?
faqs.answer: No. He says “if you’re a baby, you’re a baby, there’s nothing wrong with that,” and “God looks at you and says that person is perfect” because “they’re right where they’re supposed to be at this time.”

faqs.question: Does he say Christians should see a doctor?
faqs.answer: Yes. He says “God can heal, but if he doesn’t, you better get to a doctor,” citing Jesus: “They that are sick need a physician.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: When Jesus heard that, He said to them, “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick.

faqs.question: What does he say about welfare?
faqs.answer: He says “welfare is a bribe,” that it “should be connected with work,” and that “somebody has got to get this,” while saying “is there a time where people need help? Absolutely.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: But if anyone does not provide for his own, and especially for those of his household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.

faqs.question: What does he say it means to be a “baby Christian”?
faqs.answer: He says “if you are number two … you are a born-again, probably a baby Christian, and there’s nothing wrong with being a baby Christian at all.”

faqs.question: How much time does he say God asks for each day?
faqs.answer: He says “God asks for one hour of your day,” “in the Bible and in prayer,” and that people have “time to watch everything on TV” but are “busy satisfying your own agenda.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I also will reject you from being priest for Me; Because you have forgotten the law of your God, I also will forget your children.
